primitives.name: Signal Taxonomy Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: Signal taxonomy (11 signals) Every paper carries ≥0 signal tags (pure-theory papers legitimately carry none — never invented).
primitives.assumptions: Each paper is tagged with zero or more of 11 discrete signal types; pure theory papers are excluded from invention.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a paper lacks any invented signal, it is classified as theoretical and not part of the actionable corpus.

layer2.mapping: Each signal tag corresponds to a distinct kernel in GSE's state-space model, enabling modular composition of predictive architectures.
layer2.telemetry: Cross-validation accuracy of signal-tagged subsets against known outcomes.

primitives.name: Lane Normalization Map
primitives.verbatim_quote: Lane normalization map The tracker accumulated 50+ raw lane spellings.
primitives.assumptions: Multiple spelling variants exist for lane names; normalization ensures consistent indexing.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Mislabeling occurs when raw lane terms do not align with canonical definitions.

layer2.mapping: Normalizes raw lane strings into standardized categories for downstream signal tagging and bucket assignment.
layer2.telemetry: Frequency of suggested_lane corrections made by indexer.

primitives.name: Suggested Lane Judgment
primitives.verbatim_quote: Each record also carries `suggested_lane` — the indexer's judgment call, used to catch tracker mislabels (e.g., Kelly papers filed under `win_spread_total`, stock-sentiment papers filed under `markets`).
primitives.assumptions: Indexer judgment improves classification accuracy by correcting tracker errors.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Misclassification rate exceeds acceptable threshold when suggested_lane differs from tracker_lane.

layer2.mapping: Provides corrective feedback loop for lane assignment, enhancing signal taxonomy integrity.
layer2.telemetry: Percentage of records where suggested_lane differs from tracker_lane.
